Upon an application filed by the respondent herein, a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was drawn up and the learned Magistrate after final hearing found the possession of the land relating to which proceeding under Section 145 Cr . PC was initiated as of the 151 party i.e. the respondent and thereupon directed the receiver to handover possession of the land to the 1" party in the proceeding. As against the said order of the learned Magistrate 2"' party i.e. petitioners herein filed Criminal Motion before the Court of Sessions Judge, Chittagong and the said revision was heard by the learned Additional District Judge who set aside the order dated 15th June, 1997 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 244 of 1973 of the Court of Thana Magistrate, Banshkhali, Chittagong . The party as against the order of the learned Additional District Judge moved the High Court Division by filing an application under Section 56IA of the Cr . PC and obtained the Rule. A Division Bench of the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record upon arriving at the finding that 1'r party by independent witness proved his claim of possession in the land relating to which proceeding was initiated under section 145 Cr. PC and that order of the Magistrate making direction to the receiver to handover possession of the land in the proceeding to the 1" party was based on due consideration of the evidence on record "and as such there is no scope of arriving at a different conclusion on consideration of some documents as was done by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in the revision" quashed the order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge reversing the order of the learned Magistrate. 

 reaching finality of the proceeding that was initiated sometime in 1973 and that the property during this period remained with the receiver. Merely because of the lapse of time it cannot be said that apprehension of imminent breach of peace over the possession of the land in the proceeding started sometime in 1973 has disappeared and that the proceeding lost its efficacy, rather the question of possession as has been decided by the court maintaining thereof would remove the apprehension of the breach of peace which is being postulated by the provisions of Section 145 Cr. Pc. The other contention that the High Court Division was in error in giving preference to the oral evidence over the documentary evidence is also of no substance since the oral evidence relating to the question of possession of the land in the proceeding shall have always precedence over the documents containing any statement of fact as to possession of the land in the proceeding since veracity of the oral evidence is considered in the light of the statements made in the course of cross-examination as well as upon the demeanour of the witness. In the instant case it is seen from the materials on record that the I' party by the evidence of the witnesses who are neighbour to the land has proved his possession in the land- in the proceeding and as against that the 2nd party has not adduced any evidence to dislodge the evidence of the said witnesses. Since the order. relating to possession of the land that has been made by the learned Magistrate is based of the evidence of the reliable witnesses and consequent thereupon order directing the receiver to handover possession of the land to the party is, in our view legally sustainable and as such the High Court Division has committed no error in setting aside the order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge reversing the order of the learned Magistrate. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.
